plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $20, the expected value of the maximum of two other bids is approximately 2/3 * 20 = $13.33. To win with high probability, I'll bid slightly above this, accounting for the risk of losing to a very high value. Given my value of $34, bidding $13.40 is a safe, maximizing bid.

Since all bidders are rational, and values are between $0 and $20, a dominant strategy exists. Bidding your true value is *not* optimal. The optimal strategy is to bid slightly above zero, aiming to win only when the item is worth more than the second-highest bid. Given my value of $33 (which is irrelevant since the maximum possible value is $20), I will bid a small amount to try and win at the lowest possible price. I'll bid $0.1.
